verdicts.strongest_argument: The hunter's own independence citation publishes the finding. A participant in the captured stream wrote on 2026-07-21, six weeks before the print, 'stock trading at 17$, meaning it dropped below the 18$ price of the recent share issuance. This will head back above as soon as the company releases info on the new acquisition' - which is the deal-buyers-underwater observation, the undeployed-cash observation and the mean-reversion conclusion, all in one sentence, in the same document the finding rests on (docs/170806f7b3373558655fba2c2c0b8739efd7da18.txt). The offering itself is a 424B5 with an S-3ASR in filings.json and the pricing, size and bookrunners are in the captured body at the 2026-06-30 entries, so every input is public. The remaining step - comparing $15.96 to $18.00 - is subtraction on two published numbers. And the price has done the work: the announcement day fell 12.3% and the twenty sessions into the print are -12.83% per the baseline, so the market has already marked the equity below the placement price rather than failing to notice it is there. The 'institutional book is the marginal holder' mechanism also has no direction: a book that is underwater sells as readily as it averages down, and nothing in the capture says which. The 'can't find a reason for the drop' quote from 2026-08-27 is a retail participant's puzzlement, not evidence of unpriced information.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The finding is that an 8-K exists whose contents nobody knows, and I think the most likely contents make it empty. An 8-K carrying items 1.01, 8.01 and 9.01 filed on 2026-07-01, the day after a marketed secondary closed, is the textbook filing for the underwriting agreement itself: the underwriting agreement is a material definitive agreement (1.01), the closing or pricing press release goes under 8.01, and the agreement plus opinion are the 9.01 exhibits. That reading explains the item combination, the date and the absence of any coverage far better than an unannounced acquisition, and if it is right the filing is a mechanical adjunct to an event that is already fully published - which is why I put this at the midpoint rather than in the reachable-but-unconnected band. The finding's alternative readings do not help it either: a credit facility signed alongside a raise is routine and a purchase agreement would have been announced, because a company that raised $100m explicitly to fund acquisitions has every incentive to disclose one and the retail base is on record nine weeks later still waiting. The hunter concedes the direction is uncertain and that this collapses into #0's source cluster. What keeps me from going higher is honest: the body is not stored, so I cannot prove my reading, and the corpus cannot resolve it either way.
